messages.author: 22583a676ffdcbde
messages.subject: How can I pass more backend parameters in rmr
parts:
Greetings.

I want to pass both number of mappers and mapred.task.timeout values as backend parameters in mapreduce API. But I am not able to do that. Both the values are required since I am running a CPU intensive simulations which will take atleast 30 mins to complete. Apart from setting the cluster value Is there anything that I can pass it via mapreduce API?

Example code that I have tried is,

mapreduce.output = from.dfs(mapreduce(paste("/tmp",filePath,sep="/"),map=map.tam,reduce=reduce.tam,input.format="text",backend.parameters = list(hadoop = list(D = "mapred.task.timeout=3600000"),hadoop = list(D = 'mapred.map.tasks=4'))))

but it doesnt seem to be working.

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#331] How can I pass more backend parameters in rmr
parts:
The syntax is slightly wrong, it should be

backend.parameters = list(hadoop = list(D = ..., D = ..., ...))

With the .. replaced by the same key value pairs you specified. But I also have to warn you that you are working at an edge case of Hadoop and it may not be the best tool for the job. Could you rephrase your computation into slightly smaller chunks even at the cost of creating some redundant input? You can have as input the iteration number for instance, even if you don't need it. 


Antonio

messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#334] How can I pass more backend parameters in rmr
parts: So what I gathered from people who know Hadoop better than I do is that having a very high timeout is not a good idea and will impact fault tolerance and utilization. But I think I have found a potential workaround, based on the status string update. If one updates the status string the timeout clock is restarted. So if you have a very long computation that generates only one record of output, one solution may be to update the job status from time to time. This is not currently possible in rmr, that's why I said "potential", but we could enter a feature proposal and see if somebody takes it on.

On Nov 8, 2012 12:09 AM, "Antonio Piccolboni" <ant...@piccolboni.info> wrote:
I reopened https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RHadoop/issues/14 to keep track of progress on this feature. It looks like it is enough to print to standard error 

reporter:status:<message>

In R that would be achieved with 

cat("reporter", "status", some.message, sep =":", file = stderr())

I suspect this should happen often enough to beat the timeout but not too often so as not to burden the system (the status update is a centralized feature and won't scale to millions of updates, I think).
